ai.title: Add HMAC-shielded account deletion proof for Convex purges
ai.summary: The `common` utility `account-deletion-proof.ts` introduces `createAccountDeletionProof` and `verifyAccountDeletionProof`, which derive an HMAC-SHA256 over a payload that length-prefixes the `PROOF_VERSION`, identity subject, and deletion code so each field cannot collide in the encoded string. The signing secret must be at least 32 characters, and verification uses a constant-time comparison over fixed-size hex signatures. As noted in the JSDoc, the proof is minted only after Adbuff reports an active suppression fence and is presented on each bounded Convex purge pass, never returned to the browser.

ai.title: Mid-turn /plan /interview /review and /skill queue instead
ai.summary: The `/plan`, `/interview`, and `/review` commands previously called `sendMessage()` directly without checking whether a run was in progress, which forced `registerActiveRun` to stop the in-flight run (root cause: a user report in #1211 where a mid-turn message overwrote the active job instead of queuing). This commit routes all of those - plus `/skill:<name>` - through `dispatchSkillPrompt`, which mirrors the busy-check-then-queue-else-send logic already used by `/skill:<name>` inline args, so a mid-turn submit waits its turn instead of interrupting. A new `cli/src/utils/steering-buffer.ts` mailbox lets the router echo a bubble immediately and hand mid-turn plain text to the active run at its next step boundary, falling back to the queue for anything steering can't carry (attachments, slash commands, pending bash output, a non-empty queue, or no active run). `use-send-message.ts` wires `activateSteering`, `drainSteeringMessages`, and `deactivateSteering` into the SDK run lifecycle via `RunOptions.drainSteeringMessages` and a new `pauseQueue` option, so undelivered steering text is retracted and requeued rather than lost. There are six other supporting changes in the same area: `prompt-builders.ts` adds `buildSkillPrompt` for byte-identical prompts across the args and input-mode entry paths; `chat-store.ts` adds `pendingSkillName`, `setPendingSkillName`, and `enterSkillMode`; `input-modes.ts` adds a `skill` mode config; `chat-input-bar.tsx` labels the skill-mode banner with the pending skill name; `status-bar.tsx` renders context usage via a new `format-token-count.ts`; and `chat.tsx` passes `hasQueuedMessages` through to the router.

ai.title: Fix totalTokens double-counting cacheReadTokens in usage types
ai.summary: Updated `FreebuffRecentUsage` in `common/src/types/freebuff-usage.ts` to clarify that `totalTokens` equals `inputTokens + outputTokens`, explicitly excluding `cacheReadTokens` from the sum. This prevents ~1.8x inflation of token counts at high cache hit rates, as `cacheReadTokens` is a subset of `inputTokens` rather than an additive component. The change affects shared core types used by UI tiles and usage reporting surfaces.

eli5.text: The assistant's usage screen was showing a number that was too high, so the math was corrected. The total token count now adds up only the words you typed and the words the assistant wrote, instead of also re-counting the portion that came from the shortcut memory. You might notice the usage numbers on your dashboard tiles read a bit lower than before, especially when a lot of the work is being pulled from the memory cache. The correction prevents the system from counting the cached portion twice, which previously inflated the totals by roughly 80% during heavy cache use. This fix is live now across the shared usage types that power those tiles and reports, so the figures you see today should reflect the corrected calculation.

facts: Markdown by default (same rendering as `/copy` via serializeConversation); a filename ending in `.json` exports the raw message objects instead, using the persistence-safe serializer so cyclic tool output can't throw.
Async on purpose: a multi-MB transcript flushed synchronously would block the CLI's render/input thread (the same reason writeFileAtomicAsync exists for the checkpoint writer).
Never clobber: the atomic write renames over the target, so an existing file, `/export README.md` from a slip or tab-complete, would be destroyed with no prompt and no backup.
Inside the try: a multi-MB transcript can throw from serialization itself (RangeError: Invalid string length), and that must surface as an ExportResult error rather than an unhandled rejection.
